How to get a death certificate in Australia (Qld, NSW and Victoria)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 9 Nov 2026

Usually the funeral director registers the death and orders the death certificate for the family. If you need one yourself, apply to the Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages in the state or territory where the death was registered, with proof of identity and proof you're eligible. In Queensland, NSW and Victoria eligible applicants include the spouse or partner, parent or child; Queensland and NSW also list the executor. Each registry sets its own fees and processing times. In NSW a certificate costs $70 (standard) and in Victoria $59.10 plus postage.

Key facts

  • Funeral director usually orders it
  • Apply in the state where the death was registered
  • Needs proof of identity and eligibility
  • NSW $70 standard; Vic $59.10 plus postage

What are the steps?

  1. Ask the funeral director first. NSW and Victoria both say the funeral director normally registers the death and orders the certificate for you; in NSW they register it within 7 days of the burial or cremation.
  2. Apply to the registry where the death was registered. Queensland's service is only for deaths registered in Queensland; for a death elsewhere, apply in that state, territory or country.
  3. Check you're eligible. Queensland: the spouse, parent or child, the person who signed the death registration, the funeral director, or an executor. NSW: a spouse or de facto partner, parent or child whose details are on the certificate, the funeral director (within 30 days of registration), the executor or the estate's solicitor. Victoria: next of kin (spouse or domestic partner, child or parent), or others with third party authority from the next of kin.
  4. Gather proof of identity. Queensland asks for 3 forms of ID including proof of home address, as certified copies if you post the application. Victoria lets you verify your identity online with two documents, or with certified copies. NSW requires proof of identity with every application.
  5. Apply. Queensland: online form, then post the documents or submit in person at a Queensland Magistrates Court or QGAP office (not Brisbane Magistrates Court) or at the Brisbane registry. NSW: online, by post or at a Service NSW centre. Victoria: apply online through BDM Victoria.
  6. Pick the right certificate. Queensland's official death certificate shows the cause of death and is used to finalise estate matters; a limited certificate may not be accepted everywhere. NSW warns that an extract certificate may not be accepted by some organisations. Victoria's package includes certificates with and without the cause of death.
  7. Use the official registry website. NSW warns that third-party websites offering to process certificate applications aren't affiliated with the Registry.
  8. Banks, super funds, telcos and the ATO will ask for the death certificate (often a certified copy), so use our guides to work through each one.

Frequently asked questions

Who can get a death certificate in Australia?

It depends on the state. Queensland: the spouse, parent or child, the person who signed the death registration, the funeral director or an executor. NSW: a spouse or de facto partner, parent or child named on the certificate, the funeral director (within 30 days of registration), the executor or the estate's solicitor. Victoria: the next of kin, or others with their written authority.

How much does a death certificate cost?

NSW charges $70 for standard service and $105 for priority, both including $11 postage and handling. Victoria charges $59.10 for a death certificate (with or without the cause of death) or $95.80 for a package of both, plus $10.60 express post within Australia. Queensland's fee is shown when you apply.

How long does it take to get a death certificate?

NSW: up to 1 week for a death registration and certificate, or up to 3 weeks for a standard online application (2 weeks priority), plus 5 to 7 days for delivery. Victoria: up to 7 days for a registration and certificate in the last 3 months, otherwise up to 14 days, plus postage.

Does the funeral director get the death certificate?

Usually. NSW and Victoria both say the funeral director normally registers the death and applies for the certificate on the family's behalf.

Can I get a death certificate if I'm not family?

Sometimes. In NSW you need a letter of authority from someone recorded on the certificate (with their ID and yours) or evidence of an interest in the estate. In Victoria you need third party authority from the next of kin. Queensland lists who else can apply and the documents they need.

Which death certificate do I need for the estate?

In Queensland, the official death certificate, which shows the cause of death and is used to finalise estate matters. Limited or extract certificates may not be accepted by all organisations.
